note: Cook Islands, read on 2026-10-30 in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration's 'COVID 19 – Policy on Permits' of 2 April 2020 (published on the Ministry of Internal Affairs' site, intaff.gov.ck), the latest of the Ministry's own texts that could be read: the Ministry's current pages (mfai.gov.ck) answer with a Cloudflare bot check, which wasn't passed. Its definitions: a work permit is for a person who isn't a Cook Islander or permanent resident and lives in the Cook Islands for employment or business; residence is for one living there through a relationship with a Cook Islander or permanent resident, work permitted (work any); an entry permit is for the spouse, child or other family member of a work permit holder, no work permitted (work none); a permanent resident is one on whom the Cook Islands has conferred that status. Cook Islanders are those within the Entry, Residence and Departure Act's definition. The policy's fees (before 24 March 2020 $40 a month and a $20 application fee; a year's extension $400 plus $20; a $250 fee to transfer from one employer to another; elsewhere $500 a year) were set for the pandemic's relief and don't agree with each other, so no fee is written; currency New Zealand dollars. No term, decision time or years to permanent residence are stated. The Immigration Act 2021, which may have changed these permits, wasn't read (the Cook Islands' legislation on PacLII sits behind a bot check), so this file shows the permits as the Ministry defined them in 2020.
